name: Vectron
summary: A compiler pass that analyses array- and matrix-based dynamic programming kernels and vectorizes them automatically, reporting up to 18x throughput improvement on DP algorithms. Vectron is written as a Codon extension: its 151 .codon files carry the dispatcher, the attribute machinery and a large set of generated CPU and GPU alignment kernels, and it depends on a from-source Codon build with its LLVM distribution.
why_codon: Vectron is built as a Codon compiler pass; the repo states the vectorizer improves DP performance up to 18 times.

paper.title: Vectron: A Dynamic Programming Auto-vectorization Framework

name: FLOX
summary: A framework for building trading systems -- strategies, backtests, paper trading and live execution behind one toolkit, distributed on PyPI and npm. Codon is the scripting surface over a C or C++ core rather than the whole system: 55 .codon files hold the strategy, backtest, order-book and execution modules, and 28 of them declare 1,347 C entry points through Codon's from-C-import interop.
why_codon: Repo makes no explicit Codon performance claim; the binding layer implies Codon is used for native-speed strategy code over the C API.

name: Conduit
summary: A web framework for machine-learning APIs, MCP servers and streaming services, describing itself as AI-first and claiming native performance. Codon is the implementation language: 151 .codon files hold the HTTP server, middleware, MCP protocol handling and tooling, with sockets bound through from-C-import and a NumPy path used for the inference demos.
why_codon: Repo claims native performance for a Python-shaped web framework; badge pins Codon 0.16+.
